title: The Daily Walk With God — Micah 6:8
paragraphs: The Daily Walk With God — Micah 6:8
He’s not asking for your spotlight.

Micah 6:8 cuts through the noise like a blade:
“He has shown you, O man, what is good; and what does the Lord require of you but to do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?”
That is the daily walk with God.

Not performance.
Not religious flexing.
Not looking holy while your heart stays untouched.

Do justly.
That means you tell the truth when lying would protect you.
You treat people right when no one is watching.
You stop using power to wound and start using it to serve.

Love mercy.
Not tolerate mercy.
Not talk about mercy.
Love it.
Because if we are honest, every one of us is standing today because God did not give us what our sins deserved. In Christ, mercy is not a weak thing. Mercy is blood-bought. Mercy has nail marks.

Walk humbly with your God.
That is the secret.
Not rushing ahead of Him.
Not dragging His name behind your plans.
Walking with Him. Daily. Quietly. Faithfully.
A surrendered life is louder in heaven than a thousand empty religious words.

But here’s what we miss: Micah 6:8 is not God handing sinners a ladder to climb into His love. It is God revealing the kind of life that flows from a heart brought low before Him. And none of us have walked this perfectly. We have failed justice. We have withheld mercy. We have chosen pride.
That is why we need Jesus.

Jesus is the truly just One.
Jesus is mercy in the flesh.
Jesus walked in perfect humility before the Father, then went to the cross for proud, unjust, mercy-needing people like us. Through His death and resurrection, He does not just forgive us. He changes us. He teaches us to walk.

So today, don’t just ask, “What do I need to achieve for God?”
Ask, “Lord, how do I walk with You today?”

One step of obedience.
One act of mercy.
One surrendered heart.

Prayer:
Lord, teach me to do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with You. Expose my pride. Cleanse my heart through Jesus Christ. Let my daily life reflect Your truth, Your compassion, and Your grace. Amen.
